impact: A relief bounce in the memory names that drive MU, DRAM and SNXX sentiment, but it recovers only part of Wednesday's losses. A higher Korean policy rate is a mild headwind for SKM.
summary: Asian chip stocks led a rebound on Thursday after Wednesday's crash, when the Kospi fell 6.16% to 4,697.51 and the Taiex 4.8%. Late in the session AP had the Kospi up 1.2% at 4,755.29 and the Taiex up 2.6%; the Nikkei 225 rose about 1.2% to 1.7% depending on the report. SK Hynix rose 3.7% after being up as much as 5.5% in the morning, while Kioxia and SoftBank jumped by double digits. CNBC said the Bank of Korea raised its policy rate to 3.25%. Analysts cautioned the bounce may be a short-lived relief rally. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving.
title: Asia rebounds after chip rout: Taiex up 2.6%, Kospi 1.2%, SK Hynix 3.7%; Bank of Korea hikes
